an_empty_section_is_distinguishable_from.description: The output has four list sections (REQ, NAMED, TRACE) and two counters. A section that emitted nothing is indistinguishable from a section whose code never ran -- the same absence-versus-zero problem as a census with no denominator. Here it bites hardest on TRACE and on UNSET.
an_empty_section_is_distinguishable_from.expected_landed: a COUNTS line stating req_lines, named_lines, trace_lines and whether any traceback was left unterminated, so each list's length is asserted independently of the list itself
an_empty_section_is_distinguishable_from.expected_not_landed: a silent empty section, where 0 TRACE lines could mean no traceback, or a traceback the program failed to close
an_empty_section_is_distinguishable_from.observed: COUNTS req_lines=3 named_lines=9 trace_lines=0 unterminated_traceback=0. The 3 and the 9 equal the lines actually printed. trace_lines=0 agrees with tracebacks=0 on the WINDOW line, which is an independent substring count, and unterminated_traceback=0 says the zero is not a traceback whose last line fell outside the window. So 0 TRACE lines means the resident raised nothing in this window, which is a finding in its own right: run 4 was refused, not crashed.

nothing_was_written_to_the_host.description: The bounds say NO WRITE TO THE HOST. The obvious implementation -- dump journalctl to a temp file and grep it several times -- writes to /tmp, which is a write, and also reads a slightly different window per grep so the counts need not agree with each other.
nothing_was_written_to_the_host.expected_landed: ONE journalctl read piped into ONE awk, no temp file, no redirection to any host path, and every count derived from the same single pass
nothing_was_written_to_the_host.expected_not_landed: any file created on the host, or counts computed from separate journalctl invocations
nothing_was_written_to_the_host.observed: The command contains exactly one journalctl invocation, piped directly into awk; the only redirection in the whole script is the pipe. No temp path appears in it. Every number on the WINDOW, COUNTS, UNSET and SENDFAIL lines comes from the same 165-line pass, so they are mutually consistent by construction. The command also contains no write verb at all -- no systemctl start/stop/restart, no aws sqs receive/delete, no dynamodb call, no secret read, no vendor call.

the_window_in_time_is_stated_and_the_tz_.observed: hosttz=+0000, printed by date +%z on the host in the same command, and every journal timestamp in the output carries +0000 independently. So the --since 2026-10-11 11:15:00 window IS the 11:15:00Z window. The run-4 submission is recorded by the issuer at 11:19:00Z, four minutes inside it, and the window's own first REQ line is at 11:19:02 -- consistent.
